solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The quick way/express route?

parts.note: fleet means swift or quick, as in fleet of foot
a street is a road or way

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the fastest road to take, the express route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' hides a capital: the Daily Express newspaper was long based on this London street, the old home of the British press.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Express had its offices on this London street of newspapers, so it was that paper's route or address.

clue.text: Midweek, same cafe, turns up wearing this?

definitions.text: Midweek, same cafe, turns up wearing this?

indicators.note: turns up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the opening words wear the item, carrying it within their letters

explanation.surface: A regular comes into the usual cafe midweek with something covering their face.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft had no word signalling the hidden run; 'wearing this' does that job while the whole clue pictures the customer, so it is an all-in-one. 'turns up' reads the run upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue pictures a customer arriving at the cafe with nose and mouth covered, which is exactly the item worn.

clue.text: Boarded vessel securely moored?

indicators.note: securely tells us the vessel is held fast inside the other word

parts.note: to embed something is to fix it firmly in place, as a moored boat is held
an ark is a vessel, as Noah's

explanation.surface: A ship tied up firmly at the quay has passengers getting on.
explanation.definitionFit: To have boarded a ship is to have gone aboard it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: This is robbery

explanation.surface: Someone protests indignantly that this is daylight robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appears in the Financial Times, so 'This' is the paper itself, THE FT.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbery is a form of stealing, an ordinary synonym.

clue.text: Revolting, vulgar piercing? It upset Yankee jeweller

indicators.note: piercing says the reversed slang word goes through the middle of the other letters
upset means knocked over, so the two letters of it are reversed

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: revolting here means turned over, so the word for vulgar is read backwards

parts.note: naff is British slang for tacky or vulgar

explanation.surface: A tacky body piercing offends an American jeweller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' turns NAFF into FFAN; 'upset' turns IT into TI. FFAN goes into TI and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffany and Co. is a famous New York jewellery firm, and Louis Comfort Tiffany a noted designer.

clue.text: Former model in Connecticut disappeared altogether

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
the Model T was Ford's famous car
CT is the postal abbreviation for Connecticut

explanation.surface: A one-time fashion model living in Connecticut vanished without trace.
explanation.definitionFit: A species that has died out has disappeared entirely from the world.

clue.text: Band of Brothers extended quite a challenge

parts.note: tall means stretched out in height, extended
a religious order is a body of brothers, such as monks

explanation.surface: Lengthening the TV war drama Band of Brothers would be a big ask.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for a demand that is hard to meet.

clue.text: High Court strategy used by racketeer?

definitions.text: High Court strategy used by racketeer?

parts.words: High Court strategy used by racketeer?
parts.note: a racketeer here is a tennis player with a racket, and the high shot is played on court

explanation.surface: It reads like a gangster's tactics in a senior law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High Court' is not the law court but a high shot on a tennis court; 'racketeer' is someone wielding a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A lob is a high, looping shot over the opponent in tennis and similar racket games.

clue.text: Blair upset McCluskey, a collector's item!

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Len McCluskey was leader of the Unite trade union
an oil painting is a typical item for an art collector

explanation.surface: Tony Blair overturning the union leader Len McCluskey becomes a collectible moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blair' is not Tony but Lionel Blair, the British TV entertainer and dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel Blair was a well-known British dancer and television presenter, so the first name stands for him.

clue.text: He delivers cuts (except month end, late in the year)

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one

parts.words: month end, late in the year
parts.note: September to December all end in these three letters

explanation.surface: A chancellor announcing budget cuts, with the timing of the year in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: With 7 down this gives Lionel Barber, then editor of the FT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser for men delivers haircuts, so the cutter of hair is the one who delivers cuts.

clue.text: Message Cuba to return island occupied by 7 down 8

parts.note: C is the international vehicle code for Cuba

indicators.note: to return means go back, so the island name is read backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A telegram sends Cuba home an island held by the FT editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupied by 7 down 8' is extra confirmation: the island sits inside lionEL BArber, the FT editor, giving the puzzle its barber theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable is a telegram, a message sent by wire.

clue.text: Killing time before appointment with Kismet?

parts.note: something killing is deadly or fatal
an hour is a measure of time

explanation.surface: Someone idles away the time before a date with Kismet, the musical or fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet means fate, and the hour of death is a destined appointment with it.

clue.text: Author took notice of Rooney in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken, so we want what the words sound like

parts.note: took notice of is marked, and Rooney is the footballer Wayne Rooney

explanation.surface: A writer paid attention to footballer Wayne Rooney while they were chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: Wayne Rooney is a former England football captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of the American novelist Samuel Clemens, author of Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: Getting round, honours even at first

parts.note: OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour; several are OBES

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of even

explanation.surface: Someone getting around the system so that the honours come out even early on.
explanation.definitionFit: A very fat person is rotund, so round in shape is a fair synonym.

clue.text: West End comedy left 1,100 barking "Murderer!"

indicators.note: left means taken away, so those numerals are removed from the pool
barking means mad, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words are the pool
M is 1,000 and C is 100 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A London theatre comedy leaves a crowd of 1,100 yelling about a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of WEST END COMEDY less M and C, rearranged, give the demon barber of Fleet Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeney Todd is the legendary murderous barber of Fleet Street in stage and screen versions.

clue.text: Celebrated by Her Majesty, breaking open the tinnie!

definitions.note: names a birthday, the ordinal of the Queen's age in 2016

indicators.note: breaking open the can scatters its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: The Queen celebrates by cracking open a can of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: A tinnie is Australian slang for a can of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II celebrated this birthday in 2016, turning ninety.

clue.text: See 13
Makes more passionate seminal work featuring overture from Figaro

indicators.note: featuring says the opening letter appears within the reworked letters
work as a verb means knead or reshape, so the letters of seminal are reordered
the overture is the opening, so the first letter of Figaro

explanation.surface: An influential opera with the Figaro overture stirs the passions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' reorders SEMINAL into INLAMES; F goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame feelings is to arouse or intensify them, making them more passionate.

clue.text: One transferring a southern Italian chap

parts.note: signor is the Italian for Mr, a man

explanation.surface: An Italian man from the south is moving something on.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, an assignor transfers a right or property to someone else.

clue.text: We'll get this burden

definitions.meaning: a duty or responsibility one carries

explanation.definitionFit: The burden of proof is the responsibility one must carry, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Lively movements saved Chopin from schizophrenic turmoil

indicators.note: saved means rescued away, so the composer's letters are taken out
turmoil means disorder, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: the composer's letters, taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: A composer is rescued from a troubled mental state.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C,H,O,P,I,N from SCHIZOPHRENIC and rearrange the rest. Chopin did write four of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a quick, playful musical movement; the plural is lively movements.

clue.text: Turkey fesses up about conditions

indicators.note: about means around, so the confession word goes round the code

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to police
TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

explanation.surface: Turkey owns up to the terms of a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Strings attached are conditions or provisos on an offer.

clue.text: Slough pub packed, swarmed

indicators.note: packed means filled, so the pub word sits inside the other

parts.note: to slough off is to shed, as a snake does its skin
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub in the town of Slough was packed as people swarmed in.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is an English town, but here it is the verb to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: To swarm up a pole or rope is to climb it, the same as shinning up.

clue.text: Something smuggled in for Spooner's stir-crazed inmate?

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: stir is slang for prison; someone driven crazy there is mad
a lag is a convict, an old lag

explanation.surface: Contraband brought in for a prisoner going stir-crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: MAD LAG with first letters swapped gives LAD MAG, a men's magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A men's magazine is the sort of contraband smuggled into a prison.

clue.text: Slow-moving American soldier gets in trouble

indicators.note: gets in says the soldier is put inside the trouble word

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble, as in much ado
a GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A sluggish US soldier lands himself in hot water.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is a musical direction for a slow tempo.

clue.text: Poet Laureate denied high praise in book review

indicators.note: denied means refused, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a plaudit is an expression of praise
PL is the abbreviation for Poet Laureate

explanation.surface: A national poet is refused glowing praise in a literary review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book review' is not literary criticism but a check of the accounts books.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an inspection of a firm's financial records, its books.

clue.text: Election in Ohio I rigged for the rabble

indicators.note: in places the vote inside the rearranged letters
a rigged vote is fixed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a poll is an election

explanation.surface: A rigged election in Ohio is fixed for the mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi, Greek for 'the many', means the common people or masses.

clue.text: Veteran Boat Race participant lost a grand

indicators.note: lost means dropped, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Goldie is Cambridge's reserve crew, racing on Boat Race day
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: An old rower from the Boat Race loses a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an old person or thing, a veteran.

clue.text: Dependable, mature lady engaged to reverse engineer microwave component

indicators.note: engaged means held inside, so the turned letters sit within the lady

parts.note: a matron is a reliable married woman of mature years

indicators.note: reverse means read backwards

explanation.surface: A reliable older woman gets engaged to a reverse engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetron is the valve that generates the microwaves in a microwave oven.

clue.text: Wicked individual's criminal pattern discovered in study

indicators.note: discovered in means found within the other word

parts.note: a den is a private room or study
MO is modus operandi, a criminal's usual method

explanation.surface: A villain's method is uncovered in the course of a study.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil spirit, or figuratively a wicked person.

clue.text: Fluid, unknown departure from Maltese island

indicators.note: departure from means the letter leaves the island's name

parts.note: Gozo is the second island of Malta
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A fluid, uncertain exit from an island near Malta.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is a sticky or viscous liquid substance.

clue.text: Musical actor's wardrobe assistant and stylist

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a dresser helps an actor with costumes backstage

explanation.surface: A stage show's costume helper doubles as its hair stylist.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair stylist is another name for one who cuts and styles hair.
